hooks.text: Stop scrambling all week long. Here's how independent creators batch their weekly content planning so you actually have time to create instead of plan.
One session, seven posts done. Learn the three-step system that lets you build your entire weekly feed before the week even starts.
If you're drowning in content ideas but running out of time, skip the guesswork. Watch how to batch your weekly planning in under five minutes.

sections.heading: Intro / Hook
sections.text: One session, seven posts done. Learn the three-step system that lets you build your entire weekly feed before the week even starts.

sections.heading: Step 1 — Capture & Cluster Ideas
sections.text: First, spend 15 minutes gathering everything that sparks your creativity this week—notes, photos, voice memos. Then group them by theme. This simple clustering turns scattered thoughts into a manageable list.

sections.heading: Step 2 — Map the Grid
sections.text: Next, map your grid. Decide which platform formats fit best—Reels, carousels, static posts—and assign each idea to a specific slot. Seeing the whole week laid out prevents last-minute scrambling.

sections.heading: Step 3 — Batch Produce
sections.text: Finally, create in batches. Shoot all your videos together, take all your photos, then design your captions. Doing each task once saves hours of context-switching.

sections.heading: Outro / CTA
sections.text: Try this system this week and watch your creative energy return. Follow for more practical creator hacks.

feedback: The script fully meets the brief: three concrete steps (Capture & Cluster, Map the Grid, Batch Produce), no invented performance statistics, and maintains a friendly, direct, practical tone suitable for independent creators.
The selected hook (hook_2) effectively introduces the core value proposition ('One session, seven posts done') while staying grounded in the actual method rather than overpromising.
All three steps are actionable and distinct, providing clear guidance without fabricated metrics.
The structure (Intro → Step 1 → Step 2 → Step 3 → Outro) aligns well with the 45-second target, and the production notes support a tight pacing approach.
No substantive corrections are needed—the script is ready for production.
